title: Understanding Elastic Collisions
text: In an elastic collision, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. This means that the total kinetic energy before the collision is equal to the total kinetic energy after the collision.

title: Using Conservation of Momentum
text: The conservation of momentum can be expressed as: $$m_{1}v_{1i}+m_{2}v_{2i}=m_{1}v_{1f}+m_{2}v_{2f}.$$ Here, $$m_{1}$$ and $$m_{2}$$ are the masses of the alpha particle and uranium nucleus, respectively, and $$v_{1}$$ and $$v_{2}$$ are their velocities.

title: Using Conservation of Kinetic Energy
text: Since the uranium nucleus is initially stationary, $$v_{2i}=0$$.

title: Calculating the Final Velocities
text: Using the conservation equations, solve for the final velocities of the alpha particle and the uranium nucleus.

title: Finding the Kinetic Energy Transferred
text: Calculate the kinetic energy transferred to the uranium nucleus using the formula: $$KE_{\text{transferred}}=0.5m_{2}v_{2f}**{2}$$.

title: Calculating the Percent of Kinetic Energy Transferred
text: The percent of kinetic energy transferred is given by: $$(KE_{\text{transferred}}/KE_{\text{initial}})\times100,$$ where $$KE_{\text{initial}}$$ is the initial kinetic energy of the alpha particle.
